name: ABC
question: Does one 100 U intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA injection reduce urgency incontinence episodes differently from a six-month oral anticholinergic regimen in women with idiopathic urgency urinary incontinence?

arms.label: OnabotulinumtoxinA 100 U intradetrusor injection with oral placebo
oral solifenacin with escalation or a switch to trospium XR, plus saline injection

design.population: 249 randomized women without neurologic disease who had five or more urgency incontinence episodes per 3-day diary, were anticholinergic-naive or had used up to two anticholinergics other than solifenacin, darifenacin or trospium, and had a postvoid residual below 150 mL.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, double-placebo randomized superiority trial
design.locator: PMC3543828 Methods, Study Design; Results, Participants; Figure 1

verdictNote: Episode reduction did not differ; complete resolution favored toxin, while urinary infection and catheterization were more frequent.
takeaway: In women with idiopathic urgency urinary incontinence, one 100 U onabotulinumtoxinA injection and six months of oral solifenacin (with escalation or a switch to trospium XR) reduced daily episodes similarly (3.3 versus 3.4 fewer); toxin gave more complete resolution but more urinary infection and catheterization.

reports.label: Published protocol
reports.citation: Visco AG, Brubaker L, Richter HE, et al. "Anticholinergic versus Botulinum Toxin A Comparison Trial for the Treatment of Bothersome Urge Urinary Incontinence: ABC Trial." *Contemp Clin Trials.* 2012;33(1):184-196. doi:10.1016/j.cct.2011.09.019
reports.followUp: Protocol description; no outcome data

delivery.label: Injection technique
delivery.value: Wolf injection cystoscope with the bladder filled with 100 to 200 mL; 10 mL containing 100 U onabotulinumtoxinA (or placebo) plus 0.1 mL indigo carmine injected at about 15 to 20 detrusor sites under direct vision with disposable needles, covering the posterior wall and dome and sparing the trigone, ureteral orifices and anterior dome, followed by a 1 mL saline flush.

delivery.label: Preinjection requirements
delivery.value: Negative dipstick urinalysis (below 1+ nitrite and below 1+ leukocyte) before injection; ineligible if postvoid residual was 150 mL or more on two occasions; patient or caregiver confirmed able to perform clean intermittent self-catheterization before randomization.

reports.label: Six-month randomized comparison
reports.citation: Visco AG, Brubaker L, Richter HE, et al. "Anticholinergic Therapy vs. OnabotulinumtoxinA for Urgency Urinary Incontinence." *N Engl J Med.* 2012;367(19):1803-1813. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1208872
reports.followUp: Mean change over months 1 to 6 of the double-blind phase; off-treatment follow-up to month 12

results.measure: Adjusted mean reduction in urgency incontinence episodes per day averaged over months 1 to 6 (baseline mean 5.0 per day); 241 women analyzed
results.locator: PMC3543828 Results, Efficacy; Figure 2
results.note: Powered to detect a difference of 0.8 episodes per day (SD 2.1, 80% power, two-sided alpha 0.05 with one interim look); the report gives P only for the between-group comparison. 9% of monthly diaries were missing.

results.measure: Complete resolution of urgency incontinence among women returning at least four follow-up diaries

delivery.label: Treatment regimen
delivery.value: Solifenacin 5 mg daily, raised to 10 mg at month 2 and switched to trospium XR 60 mg at month 4 when control was inadequate and side effects tolerable, plus a saline injection; or one 100 U intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA injection plus placebo pills escalated on the same schedule.

delivery.label: Catheterization rule
delivery.value: Intermittent catheterization for postvoid residual above 300 mL, or above 150 mL when the participant rated it moderately or quite bothersome.

delivery.value: 249 randomized (127 anticholinergic, 122 toxin), 247 treated (126 and 121), 241 in the primary analysis; baseline mean 5.0 urgency incontinence episodes per day and 41% anticholinergic-naive.

name: Sun acupuncture for CP/CPPS
question: Does acupuncture improve symptoms more than sham acupuncture in men with moderate to severe chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome?

design.blinding: Participants, outcome assessors, and statisticians blinded; acupuncturists unblinded
design.population: 440 men aged 18 to 50 years with moderate to severe chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome (NIH-CPSI at least 15) at ten tertiary hospitals in China.
design.description: Multicenter, randomized, sham-controlled superiority trial
design.locator: Full text, Methods, Setting and Participants, p 1358; Figure 1, p 1359

verdictNote: Prespecified responder tests were significant at weeks 8 and 32 in intention-to-treat analysis.
takeaway: Among 440 men with moderate to severe chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome, 20 acupuncture sessions over 8 weeks increased modeled NIH-CPSI response versus sham at weeks 8 and 32 (adjusted OR 2.6 at both time points).

name: ALFAUR
question: Does alfuzosin before catheter removal improve trial without catheter success after a first BPH-related acute urinary retention episode?

design.population: 363 men older than 50 years with a first episode of spontaneous acute urinary retention attributed to benign prostatic hyperplasia and 500–1500 mL drained at emergency catheterization were randomized; 360 received first-phase treatment.
design.description: Double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial at 71 centers in Europe and South Africa with second-phase rerandomization
design.locator: Full text (2005 report), Methods, p 84; Table I, p 85

verdictNote: The initial voiding-trial endpoint improved; six-month surgery incidence did not differ significantly.
takeaway: After emergency catheterization for first BPH-related acute urinary retention, alfuzosin 10 mg once daily before catheter removal improved successful voiding versus placebo (146/236 [61.9%] versus 58/121 [47.9%]; P = 0.012); six-month surgery incidence after rerandomization did not differ significantly.

reports.label: Initial voiding-trial report
reports.dateLocator: Crossref and PubMed give June 2004 without a day
reports.citation: McNeill SA, Hargreave TB; Members of the Alfaur Study Group. "Alfuzosin once daily facilitates return to voiding in patients in acute urinary retention." *J Urol.* 2004;171(6 Pt 1):2316-2320. doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000127743.80759.7a
reports.followUp: Catheter removed after at least two doses of blinded treatment; satisfactory voiding without recatheterization assessed within 24 hours; one additional tablet given the following day.

results.measure: Satisfactory voiding within 24 hours after catheter removal without recatheterization; no postvoid-residual threshold specified; risk difference in percentage points
results.note: Risk difference calculated from reported rounded percentages; TWOC data were available for 357 patients (236/121).
results.locator: Full text, Methods and Results, p 2317

results.endpoint: Adjusted odds of successful trial without catheter
results.measure: Alfuzosin versus placebo after adjustment for age and drained volume
results.note: Across arms, successful voiding was 49.0% at age 65 years or older versus 74.1% below 65, and 47.8% with drained volume 1,000 mL or greater versus 66.7% below 1,000 mL (both P less than 0.001). Backward logistic regression found lower odds with age 65 years or older (OR 0.309, 95% CI 0.182–0.514) and drained volume 1,000 mL or greater (OR 0.361, 95% CI 0.225–0.571); both P less than 0.0001. These prognostic analyses were not designated secondary endpoints.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 2317; Table 3, p 2318

name: Intracavernosal alprostadil
question: How did intracavernosal alprostadil perform against placebo in erectile response and during home self-injection for erectile dysfunction?

design.blinding: Double-blind placebo-controlled dose-response study; single-blind dose-finding study; open-label home-use study
design.population: Men with vasculogenic, neurogenic, psychogenic, or mixed erectile dysfunction contributed 296 dose-response, 201 dose-finding, and 683 home self-injection study enrolments; 12 dose-finding and 40 home-use participants had also joined the dose-response study.
design.description: Three prospective studies, including randomized placebo comparison
design.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 873–874; Results, pp 874–875; n is summed study enrolments, not unique patients

verdictNote: Every tested dose exceeded placebo; the home-use study was open-label.
takeaway: In a randomized, double-blind study of 296 men, intracavernosal alprostadil 2.5–20 µg produced more clinical and RigiScan erectile responses than placebo (0/59 responders). In a separate, open-label six-month study of 683 men, sexual activity was reported possible after 94% of injections.

reports.label: Dose response, dose finding, and six-month home use

name: AnTIC
aliases: Continuous low-dose antibiotic prophylaxis in clean intermittent catheter users
question: Does once-daily low-dose antibiotic prophylaxis reduce symptomatic urinary tract infections in adults using clean intermittent self-catheterisation with recurrent infections?

design.blinding: open-label; central outcome assessors and laboratory staff masked

arms.label: Once-daily nitrofurantoin, trimethoprim, or cefalexin prophylaxis

design.population: Community-dwelling adult clean intermittent self-catheterisation users with at least two symptomatic catheter-related UTIs or one UTI requiring admission in the preceding year.
design.description: Multicenter, open-label superiority randomized trial
design.locator: Full text, Methods: Study design and participants; Randomisation and masking; Results, Table 1

verdictNote: Symptomatic treated UTI incidence fell; resistant urinary isolates increased.
takeaway: In adults using clean intermittent self-catheterisation with recurrent UTI, once-daily low-dose nitrofurantoin, trimethoprim, or cefalexin reduced symptomatic antibiotic-treated UTI incidence versus no prophylaxis over 12 months (1.3 vs 2.6 per person-year; IRR 0.52); urinary bacterial resistance increased.

name: ASPIRe
aliases: Apical Suspension Repair for Vault Prolapse in a Three-Arm Randomized Trial
Apical Suspension Repair for Vaginal Vault Prolapse
question: Does sacrocolpopexy or transvaginal mesh lower composite treatment failure compared with transvaginal native-tissue suspension for vault prolapse after hysterectomy, and is vaginally placed mesh noninferior to sacrocolpopexy?

design.blinding: participants masked until surgery was completed; masked personnel performed examinations and adverse event assessments from the 6-week visit
design.population: Women aged 21 or older with symptomatic vaginal vault prolapse beyond the hymen after total hysterectomy; 376 randomized, 360 treated (arm sizes are treated participants).
design.description: Nine-center, three-arm, superiority and noninferiority randomized trial
design.locator: PDF pp1-4, Figure 1; journal pp845-848

verdictNote: Sacrocolpopexy beat native tissue; mesh was noninferior to sacrocolpopexy but missed adjusted superiority over native tissue.
takeaway: Among 360 operated women with symptomatic vault prolapse after hysterectomy, sacrocolpopexy had lower modeled 36-month composite failure than transvaginal native-tissue repair (28% versus 43%); Uphold LITE transvaginal mesh (29%) was noninferior to sacrocolpopexy but not superior to native-tissue repair after multiplicity adjustment.

reports.label: 36-month randomized report
reports.citation: Menefee SA, Richter HE, Myers D, et al. Apical suspension repair for vaginal vault prolapse: a randomized clinical trial. *JAMA Surg.* 2024;159(8):845-855. doi:10.1001/jamasurg.2024.1206
reports.followUp: Analysis when the last participant reached 36 months (July 2022); 296/360 (82%) completed follow-up

results.measure: Adjusted 36-month failure probability, sacrocolpopexy versus native-tissue repair (superiority, alpha 0.01, MITT-NTR population)
results.note: Composite of retreatment for prolapse (pessary or surgery), any POP-Q measure beyond the hymen, or any bothersome bulge on the PFDI question. 95% CIs for the failure probabilities were 20%-37% and 35%-53%. Interval-censored proportional hazards model with piecewise exponential hazards, adjusted for site and age category.

In the modified intention-to-treat population the 36-month probabilities were 29% with transvaginal mesh and 27% with sacrocolpopexy.

name: ARIA dutasteride trials
question: Does dutasteride improve symptoms and reduce acute urinary retention and BPH surgery compared with placebo in men with symptomatic enlarged prostates?

design.blinding: double-blind after a single-blind placebo lead-in
design.population: Men at least 50 years old with clinical BPH, AUA Symptom Index at least 12, Qmax at most 15 mL/s, prostate volume at least 30 cm3, and PSA 1.5–10 ng/mL; postvoid residual greater than 250 mL, AUR within 3 months, prior prostate surgery, alpha-blocker use within 4 weeks, and any prior 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor use were excluded.
design.description: Pooled, double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trials
design.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 435; Debruyne 2004 PubMed abstract, Objectives

verdictNote: The 48-month comparison was open-label; both groups received dutasteride after month 24.
takeaway: Across three randomized ARIA trials, dutasteride versus placebo improved 24-month AUA symptom score (−4.5 versus −2.3 points) and reduced acute urinary retention (39/2,167 versus 90/2,158); BPH surgery was less frequent (47/2,167 versus 89/2,158). Peak flow improved more with dutasteride in men with symptomatic enlarged prostates.

name: Barone Fistula Catheter Trial

name: BPH6
question: How does prostatic urethral lift compare with transurethral resection of the prostate for symptom relief, recovery, sexual function, continence, and safety?

design.population: Sexually active men with BPH-related lower urinary tract symptoms who were candidates for TURP, aged at least 50 years, with IPSS above 12, Qmax at most 15 mL/s, prostate volume at most 60 cc, and no obstructive median lobe or current urinary retention.
design.description: Ten-center, open-label randomized noninferiority trial
design.locator: Full text, Table 1 and Fig. 2; Study Protocol and Procedure, p 644

verdictNote: The 12-month composite favored PUL; symptom and flow gains favored TURP.
takeaway: Among 79 treated men analyzed, prostatic urethral lift was noninferior and superior to TURP on the 12-month BPH6 composite (23/44 [52%] vs 7/35 [20%]); TURP improved symptoms more, while lift favored recovery and ejaculatory preservation.

name: BRIDGE
aliases: Bridging Anticoagulation in Patients who Require Temporary Interruption of Warfarin Therapy for an Elective Invasive Procedure or Surgery
question: Does omitting perioperative low-molecular-weight heparin bridging preserve thromboembolic protection and reduce bleeding during warfarin interruption for atrial fibrillation?

design.population: Adults with atrial fibrillation or flutter receiving warfarin who required interruption for an elective operation or invasive procedure and had at least one CHADS2 stroke-risk factor.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled noninferiority randomized trial

verdictNote: No bridging met thromboembolic noninferiority and reduced major bleeding.

question: Is urethral Bulkamid injection noninferior to Contigen collagen injection for female stress urinary incontinence?

name: TVT vs PAHG
question: Is polyacrylamide hydrogel injection noninferior to retropubic tension-free vaginal tape for patient satisfaction in women with primary stress urinary incontinence?

design.population: Women with primary stress urinary incontinence unresponsive to conservative treatment, a positive cough stress test without urge-type leakage and no previous incontinence procedure.
design.description: Single-center, open-label noninferiority randomized trial
design.locator: Abstract (primary report); Methods (PMC12721665, PMC10756861)

verdictNote: Hydrogel missed the 20% satisfaction margin at 1, 3 and 5 years; complications were fewer after hydrogel.
takeaway: Polyacrylamide hydrogel (Bulkamid) injection was compared with retropubic tension-free vaginal tape in women with primary stress incontinence; 1-year satisfaction of at least 80/100 was 59.8% versus 95.0%, missing the 20% noninferiority limit, while most perioperative complications and all six complication-related reoperations followed tape.

name: CAPRICORN

design.blinding: double-blind after a single-blind placebo run-in
design.population: Adults with overactive bladder symptoms for at least three months, at least eight micturitions and three grade 3 or 4 urgency episodes per 24 hours after a two-week placebo run-in; predominant stress incontinence was excluded.

design.locator: Full text, Methods, p 314; Results, p 315

verdictNote: Both coprimary endpoints met for both doses at 12 weeks; 25 mg missed the first key secondary endpoint.
takeaway: In adults with overactive bladder, mirabegron 25 mg and 50 mg once daily improved 12-week incontinence episodes and micturition frequency versus placebo. The 50 mg dose also improved voided volume; 25 mg did not meet that key secondary endpoint.

name: CARE
question: Does adding a standardized Burch colposuspension to abdominal sacrocolpopexy reduce postoperative stress incontinence in women who are stress-continent before surgery?

design.blinding: participants, research staff and telephone interviewers masked for at least 3 months

arms.label: Abdominal sacrocolpopexy with standardized Burch colposuspension

design.description: Multicenter, masked surgical randomized superiority trial
design.locator: N Engl J Med 2006;354:1559–1561 (Methods); Fig. 2, p1560 (arm counts)

name: ChEETAh
question: Does routine change of sterile gloves and instruments before abdominal wound closure reduce 30-day surgical site infection?

design.blinding: unmasked surgical teams and outcome assessors; patients masked

arms.label: Routine change of sterile gloves and instruments before wound closure

design.population: Adults and children having emergency or elective clean-contaminated, contaminated or dirty abdominal surgery through an incision of at least 5 cm, excluding cesarean section, in 81 hospitals in seven low- and middle-income countries.
design.description: Pragmatic multicenter cluster-randomized superiority trial, hospitals randomized
design.locator: Lancet full text: Methods, Results, Figure 1

verdictNote: Adjusted RR 0.87 for 30-day SSI; the design targeted a 4-point absolute reduction.
takeaway: ChEETAh randomized 81 hospitals in seven low- and middle-income countries to routine glove and instrument change before abdominal wound closure versus current practice; 30-day surgical site infection was 16.1% versus 18.9% (adjusted risk ratio 0.87, 95% CI 0.79–0.95).

reports.citation: NIHR Global Research Health Unit on Global Surgery. results.measure: SSI within 30 days (superficial or deep incisional, CDC criteria); adjusted risk ratio

name: EMPOWUR
question: Does vibegron 75 mg once daily reduce daily micturitions and urge incontinence episodes over 12 weeks compared with placebo in adults with overactive bladder?

arms.label: tolterodine extended release 4 mg once daily

design.population: Adults with overactive bladder for at least 3 months, 85.2% women, 42.9% aged 65 or older, including up to 25% without urge incontinence.
design.description: International, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled randomized trial

verdictNote: Both co-primary endpoints met versus placebo; vibegron was not formally compared with the tolterodine reference arm.
takeaway: In adults with overactive bladder, vibegron 75 mg daily reduced daily micturitions (1.8 versus 1.3 fewer) and, with urge incontinence, its episodes (2.0 versus 1.4 fewer) more than placebo over 12 weeks; tolterodine extended release, the active reference, gave 1.6 and 1.8.

delivery.label: Voiding trial protocol

Postvoid residual >100 mL failed either method; spontaneous voided volume <200 mL was inadequate and counted as failure.

name: Ginsberg NDO

question: Does intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA reduce urinary incontinence in neurogenic detrusor overactivity, and does 300 U add benefit over 200 U?

design.population: 416 adults with urinary incontinence from neurogenic detrusor overactivity (multiple sclerosis 227, spinal cord injury 189) and 14 or more incontinence episodes per week.
design.description: International, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial

verdictNote: Both doses beat placebo; 300 U gave no clinically relevant gain and catheterization for retention rose with dose.
takeaway: In patients with neurogenic detrusor overactivity from multiple sclerosis or spinal cord injury, intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA 200 U and 300 U cut weekly incontinence episodes at week 6 by 21 and 23 versus 9 with placebo; catheterization for retention rose with dose.

name: MTOPS
question: Do doxazosin, finasteride or both together delay clinical progression of BPH in men with lower urinary tract symptoms?

design.population: 3,047 men aged 50 years or older with lower urinary tract symptoms from BPH (AUA symptom score 8 to 30 or 35, maximal flow 4 to 15 mL per second) and no prior BPH treatment.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled four-arm randomized trial
design.locator: NEJM PDF pp2-4, Table 1; journal pp2388-2390

verdictNote: Combination beat either drug alone; doxazosin did not reduce retention or invasive therapy.
takeaway: In 3,047 men with LUTS from BPH followed a mean of 4.5 years, doxazosin plus finasteride cut overall clinical progression risk by 66% versus placebo, more than doxazosin (39%) or finasteride (34%) alone; only finasteride and the combination significantly reduced acute retention and invasive therapy.

reports.label: Primary report (mean 4.5 years)
reports.citation: McConnell JD, Roehrborn CG, Bautista OM, et al. The long-term effect of doxazosin, finasteride, and combination therapy on the clinical progression of benign prostatic hyperplasia. *N Engl J Med.* 2003;349(25):2387-2398. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa030656

results.measure: Overall clinical progression, events per 100 person-years over the study (any of: confirmed AUA symptom score rise of 4 or more points, acute urinary retention, incontinence, renal insufficiency, recurrent UTI or urosepsis)
results.note: Risk reduction versus placebo (95% CI): doxazosin 39% (20 to 53; P<0.001), finasteride 34% (14 to 50; P=0.002), combination 66% (54 to 76; P<0.001); each passed the P<0.0157 threshold set for active-versus-placebo comparisons. Intention to treat; invasive BPH therapy and prostate or bladder cancer were censored as competing events.
results.locator: NEJM PDF pp3-5, Table 2; journal pp2389-2391

results.measure: Combination therapy versus each single drug, overall clinical progression over the study

results.note: Doxazosin and finasteride did not differ significantly from each other. The protocol did not specify active-versus-active comparisons; they used a Bonferroni-adjusted threshold of P<0.0167. Number needed to treat to prevent one progression event over 4 years: 8.4 for combination, 13.7 for doxazosin, 15.0 for finasteride.

name: PINNACLE
question: Does paclitaxel-coated balloon dilation of the prostatic urethra improve lower urinary tract symptoms from BPH more than a sham procedure?

arms.label: sham cystoscopic procedure with an uninflated predilation catheter

verdictNote: Primary endpoint missed with the 25% sham margin; secondary endpoints were not formally tested.
takeaway: In men with BPH-related lower urinary tract symptoms, Optilume BPH paclitaxel-coated balloon dilation improved IPSS by 11.5 points at 12 months versus 8.0 points with a sham procedure at 3 months, but missed its primary endpoint, which added a 25% margin to the sham effect.

question: Does finasteride reduce symptoms, acute urinary retention, and BPH surgery compared with placebo in men with symptomatic prostatic enlargement?

design.population: 3,040 men with moderate-to-severe urinary symptoms, low maximal urinary flow, and an enlarged prostate on digital rectal examination.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial

verdictNote: Prespecified symptom-score endpoint improved in the intention-to-treat analysis; surgery and retention were secondary endpoints.
takeaway: In 3,016 evaluable men with symptomatic prostatic enlargement, finasteride 5 mg daily for four years improved the primary symptom score (mean decrease 2.6 versus 1.0 points; P <0.001) and reduced surgery or acute retention (100/1,513 versus 199/1,503; 51% risk reduction).

name: REACTT

question: Does tadalafil started early after bilateral nerve-sparing radical prostatectomy, daily or on demand, improve unassisted erectile function after the drug is stopped?

design.population: 423 men aged 68 or younger with localized prostate cancer (Gleason score 7 or lower) and normal preoperative erectile function who underwent bilateral nerve-sparing radical prostatectomy at 50 centers in nine European countries and Canada.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, double-dummy, placebo-controlled randomized trial

verdictNote: Unassisted recovery after washout did not improve; daily tadalafil improved drug-assisted function and penile length loss.

name: RestoreX
question: Is RestoreX penile traction therapy for 30 to 90 minutes daily safe, and does it improve penile length and curvature in men with Peyronie's disease?

design.population: 110 men with Peyronie's disease (diagnosed within 10 years) and curvature of 30 degrees or more, enrolled without exclusion for complex curvature, hourglass deformity, prior Peyronie's treatment or surgery, or calcification.

name: RICH-ART
aliases: Radiation Induced Cystitis treated with Hyperbaric oxygen—A Randomised controlled Trial
question: Does hyperbaric oxygen therapy improve patient-reported urinary symptoms compared with standard care in chronic radiation-induced cystitis?

design.population: Adults aged 18–80 years referred to Nordic hyperbaric clinics with symptomatic late radiation cystitis, pelvic radiotherapy at least six months earlier, and EPIC urinary total score below 80.
design.description: Five-center, open-label, phase 2–3 randomized superiority trial
design.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 1603–1605; Results, p 1607

verdictNote: The patient-reported urinary score improved more with hyperbaric oxygen at 6–8 months.
takeaway: In the reported intention-to-treat analysis of chronic radiation cystitis, hyperbaric oxygen improved EPIC urinary total score more than standard care at 6–8 months: mean change 17.8 (n=40) versus 7.7 points (n=35), a 10.1-point difference (95% CI 2.2–18.1; p=0.013).

reports.followUp: Visit 4 at 6–8 months; median 234 days after randomization with hyperbaric oxygen and 217 days with standard care

results.endpoint: EPIC urinary total score responder status

question: How do solifenacin and oxybutynin affect short-term cognitive performance versus placebo in older adults with mild cognitive impairment?

name: SIMS
aliases: Single-Incision Mini-Slings versus Standard Midurethral Slings
question: In women undergoing primary sling surgery for stress-predominant urinary incontinence, are adjustable anchored single-incision mini-slings noninferior to standard midurethral slings for patient-reported improvement?

name: SISTEr
aliases: Stress Incontinence Surgical Treatment Efficacy Trial
question: Does an autologous rectus fascial pubovaginal sling improve continence over Burch colposuspension in women with stress-predominant urinary incontinence?

design.population: Women with pure or stress-predominant urinary incontinence, a positive stress test and urethral hypermobility; prior incontinence surgery was permitted.
design.description: Nine-center randomized surgical superiority trial with 24-month time-to-event analysis
design.locator: NEJM PDF pp2–5; journal pp2144–2147

design.population: Women aged 21 years or older, amenorrheic for at least a year and done with childbearing, who requested vaginal surgery for symptomatic uterovaginal prolapse beyond the hymen (mean age 66).
design.description: Nine-center, participant-masked randomized superiority trial of vaginal prolapse surgery
design.locator: JAMA 2019 Abstract, Methods and Statistical Analysis; Supplement 1 (protocol and SAP); AJOG 2021 Methods and Figure 1

verdictNote: Three-year difference favored mesh but missed significance (P = .06); later reports found fewer failures with mesh.
takeaway: In women with symptomatic uterovaginal prolapse, sacrospinous hysteropexy with Uphold LITE vaginal mesh did not significantly lower 36-month composite treatment failure versus vaginal hysterectomy with uterosacral ligament suspension (24% versus 36%; adjusted hazard ratio 0.61, 95% CI 0.37–1.02; P = .06); mesh exposure was 8%.

delivery.label: Mesh hysteropexy technique (Uphold LITE)
delivery.value: Hydrodissection with at least 30 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine with epinephrine or dilute vasopressin; 4 cm transverse anterior incision at least 3 cm from the cervix; extraperitoneal approach to the sacrospinous ligament; mesh delivered 1–2 fingerbreadths medial to the ischial spine; cephalic mesh edge sutured to the cervix; mesh cutting discouraged; apex resuspended without tense arms; 2-0 polyglactin closure; vaginal pack and catheter removed on postoperative day 1.

name: UPSTREAM
aliases: Urodynamics for Prostate Surgery Trial: Randomised Evaluation of Assessment Methods
question: Does adding invasive urodynamics to routine noninvasive tests before treatment decisions for bothersome male LUTS leave symptoms no worse and reduce surgery?

design.blinding: open-label; men and hospital staff unblinded; co-applicants blinded to arm throughout recruitment and analysis, junior statistician unblinded for monitoring-committee reporting

arms.label: Routine noninvasive tests plus invasive urodynamics

design.population: 820 men (median age 68) at 26 English NHS hospitals who had received conservative or medical therapy and sought further treatment, possibly including surgery, for bothersome LUTS; catheter dependence, relevant neurologic disease, prostate or bladder cancer treatment, prior prostate surgery and unfitness for surgery were excluded.
design.description: Pragmatic multicenter open-label noninferiority randomized trial
design.locator: Eur Urol accepted manuscript PDF pp4, 6-9 and Tables PDF p2 (Table 1); CONSORT PDF p2; HTA 2020 PDF pp37, 39, 42, 50

verdictNote: IPSS noninferior at 18 months, but urodynamics did not reduce the surgery rate.
takeaway: Adding invasive urodynamics to routine noninvasive tests in men with bothersome LUTS considering prostate surgery gave an 18-month IPSS noninferior to routine tests alone (adjusted difference −0.33, 95% CI −1.47 to 0.80; margin 1 point) and did not reduce surgery (38% versus 36%).

name: VUSIS-II
aliases: Value of Urodynamics prior to Stress Incontinence Surgery II
question: In women with stress-predominant incontinence and discordant urodynamic findings, is immediate sling surgery noninferior to treatment tailored to those findings?

design.blinding: Participants and clinicians unblinded; subjective outcome data entry blinded to allocation
design.population: Women with predominant stress urinary incontinence eligible for surgery on clinical assessment whose urodynamic findings were discordant with that assessment; prior incontinence surgery, prolapse at least 1 cm beyond the hymen, and postvoid residual of 150 mL or more were excluded.
design.description: Multicenter diagnostic cohort with embedded noninferiority randomized trial
design.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 1000-1001; Figure 1, p 1002

verdictNote: Noninferiority was met; 62/64 and 61/62 assigned women had sling surgery by one year.
takeaway: Among women with discordant urodynamics, immediate sling surgery was noninferior to urodynamics-guided tailored therapy for 12-month Urogenital Distress Inventory urinary-incontinence subscale improvement (44 versus 39 points; mean difference 5, one-sided 95% CI −∞ to 5); almost all women in both arms underwent sling surgery.

question: In men with symptomatic 80–180 mL prostates, is Aquablation noninferior to transurethral laser enucleation for three-month symptom improvement and procedural safety?

question: Is robotic waterjet resection (Aquablation) noninferior to TURP for relieving BPH symptoms in men with 30 to 80 mL prostates?
